title: How one explanation becomes a video
question: How do source, composition, and rendering work together?

audience.who: People authoring and reviewing explainer videos
knows: A video contains a sequence of pictures.
audience.goal: Know where to revise an explanation and how it becomes a reproducible video.

terms.name: Composition
terms.definition: The exported HTML document that contains the visual content and authored timeline.

subjects.name: HTML composition
subjects.meaning: The exported document and registered timeline.

subjects.name: Video renderer
subjects.meaning: HyperFrames captures authored times and encodes frames.

scenes.title: How editable source becomes video
scenes.description: Editable source exports an HTML composition. HyperFrames renders that composition into video.

episodes.title: Follow one composition into video
episodes.question: Where does a video get its shapes and timing?
episodes.outcome: Distinguish editable source, exported HTML, and the renderer clock.
episodes.handoff: The next episode explains the same route using a sheet-music analogy.

claims.text: The static exporter loads a default React component and writes HTML; HyperFrames renders an HTML composition using its registered paused timeline.
claims.limitation: The static exporter does not bundle animation code. A composition must supply the browser runtime, or use the new bundled graphic-video exporter.

brief.input: A TSX module with a default React component.
boundaries: The exporter writes an HTML document.
HyperFrames seeks the composition timeline and encodes video.
brief.ownership: The TSX author owns content. The exporter owns generated HTML. HyperFrames owns playback and capture timing.
brief.failure: Static markup alone does not execute client animation. Missing a registered timeline leaves the renderer without authored motion.
brief.output: An HTML composition ready for runtime validation and video rendering.

beats.title: The source owns the explanation
beats.explanation: Author the shapes, labels, and visual relationships in editable source.
beats.narration: A video begins as editable source. This is where the author chooses the shapes, labels, and relationships that explain the idea.

beats.title: Export the composition
beats.explanation: The static exporter writes the rendered component into an HTML document.
beats.narration: Export turns the component into an HTML composition. That document still needs its browser animation code and a registered timeline.

beats.title: The renderer owns time
beats.explanation: HyperFrames samples the paused timeline at authored times and encodes the captured frames.
beats.narration: HyperFrames then samples the paused timeline at authored times and encodes the frames. The renderer drives time, so seeking can revisit the same visual state.

episodes.title: A composition is like a score
episodes.question: Why keep the editable source after making the video?
episodes.outcome: Explain why editing the source preserves one explanation across rerenders.
episodes.handoff: Use the source when revising the explanation, then regenerate and review the video.

claims.text: The static exporter loads a default React component and writes HTML; HyperFrames renders an HTML composition using its registered paused timeline.
claims.limitation: The static exporter does not bundle animation code. A composition must supply the browser runtime, or use the new bundled graphic-video exporter.

brief.familiarExperience: A musician reads a score to perform a piece.
brief.goal: Understand which part to edit when the explanation changes.

correspondence.subject: source
correspondence.meaning: The author changes the source to revise the explanation.

correspondence.subject: composition
correspondence.meaning: The export is a generated copy used by the renderer.

correspondence.subject: renderer
correspondence.meaning: The renderer follows authored timing to produce the recording.

brief.analogyBreaks: A musician can improvise. Deterministic video rendering follows explicit authored timing instead.
brief.consequence: Revise the editable source, regenerate the composition, and inspect the new rendered states.

beats.title: Keep the score
beats.explanation: Editable source remains the place to revise the explanation.
beats.narration: Think of the editable source as a score. If the explanation changes, change the score so the next performance follows the same revision.

beats.title: Make a performance copy
beats.explanation: Export produces the HTML composition used for rendering.
beats.narration: The HTML composition is the performance copy. It is generated from the source and carries the visual instructions into the browser.

beats.title: Follow the authored timing
beats.explanation: The renderer produces frames from the composition at specific times.
beats.narration: The renderer performs that composition at specific times. Unlike a musician, it should not improvise. When we revisit a time, we need the same picture.
